description: An ambulatory infusion center director must decide whether to open a Sunday treatment session for a patient whose next dose is time-sensitive and finalize the medication, staffing, and transportation plan, with input from the attending physician, pharmacy, nursing, and patient transport.

shared_context.S1: The ambulatory infusion center is normally closed on Sundays.
shared_context.S2: A patient is being considered for a Sunday infusion because the weekday schedule is full.
shared_context.S3: Marisol makes the final decision about opening the Sunday session and records the operating plan.
shared_context.S4: The center's routine weekend-planning huddle includes the attending physician, pharmacy, nursing, and patient transport before any special session is finalized.

PF1.text: The attending's signed order requires this patient's infusion to run for exactly six hours and requires completion on Sunday because the next dose is due Monday at 08:00; Dr. Chen has the signed order in the clinic work queue, but the Sunday request form has not been updated.

PF2.text: The medication remains usable for exactly eight hours after compounding, and pharmacy can release the refrigerated preparation at exactly 07:30 Sunday; to preserve the labeled window, the infusion must begin at 08:00 Sunday.

PF3.text: Only RN Patel is credentialed for this medication's infusion protocol on Sunday, and Patel is available exactly from 08:00 through 14:00; the staffing roster has not yet been amended for a Sunday opening.

PF4.text: The patient's wheelchair van is reserved for a Sunday pickup exactly at 14:30, and the transport vendor has no later Sunday availability; Owen has the vendor confirmation, which is not in the center's appointment system.

acceptance_conditions: The Sunday infusion session must be opened.
The infusion must run from exactly 08:00 through 14:00 Sunday.
The medication must be released by pharmacy at exactly 07:30 Sunday.
RN Patel must be assigned for the infusion from 08:00 through 14:00.
The nursing coverage must be explicitly committed.
The patient's wheelchair van pickup at exactly 14:30 Sunday must be explicitly committed.
The attending physician's signed six-hour Sunday order must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'nursing_coverage' and c['target'] == 'Infusion Center' and c['detail'] == 'RN Patel, Sunday 08:00-14:00' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'transport_pickup' and c['target'] == 'Patient' and c['detail'] == 'wheelchair van, Sunday 14:30' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The signed order changes the plan from an optional Sunday opening to a required session ending exactly at 14:00 because the six-hour infusion must be completed Sunday before the Monday 08:00 dose.
The eight-hour post-compounding limit changes the medication release time to exactly 07:30 and the infusion start to exactly 08:00 rather than leaving either time unspecified.
The Sunday credential and availability record changes the nurse assignment to RN Patel and requires a coverage commitment for exactly 08:00-14:00.
The vendor reservation changes the transportation plan to a wheelchair-van pickup at exactly 14:30 Sunday and requires that pickup to be documented.
